scope: Classification only — no dataset is recommended for deletion. 'future status' describes how a dataset would relate to the canonical model, not an instruction to change it now.

statusDefinitions.keep: Would remain a distinct dataset even under the canonical model (e.g. a small reference table or a closed curated set).
statusDefinitions.merge: Its fields would be absorbed into the canonical Name Entity record, ending its life as a standalone file.
statusDefinitions.split: Belongs to a different entity type entirely (e.g. Surname, Country) and would migrate to a sibling schema, not this one.
statusDefinitions.derived: An upstream curation input consumed by another dataset before reaching any generator (e.g. an overrides file merged at build time).
statusDefinitions.computed: Not stored knowledge at all — a ruleset or config that computes a value at render time.
statusDefinitions.deprecated: Currently unreferenced by any script (per Phase 1B's audit/datasets.json) and its own conceptual purpose is already covered elsewhere; classification only, no deletion recommended.

datasets.note: A relational (name_id -> variant) table with 18,426 rows across 3,697 names (100% entity coverage). Overlaps data/normalized-names.json's spelling_variants[] column for the same concept — see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json.

canonicalFieldsSupplied: origin.country / origin.cluster (unenriched copy, 0% populated by construction)
datasets.secondaryOwner: meaning, origin, language (all sparse/unenriched in this file specifically)
datasets.note: The base record every other names dataset joins against by name_id. Under the canonical model this becomes the identity-domain seed of the entity record.

Currently an overlay of names.json (base fields duplicated verbatim, plus origin_cluster/origin_confidence added). Under the canonical model, origin/language become first-class fields on the one entity record — no overlay file needed.

Overlaps data/variants.json for spelling variants and data/names.json/names-enriched.json for base fields (see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json). Its unused meaning_source/origin_source/confidence_score columns are the closest thing today to the new citations domain.
A relational (name_id -> category) table today; becomes an array field on the entity record.

A curation input merged into names-enriched.json by apply-origin-enrichment.js before any generator reads it. Under the canonical model this remains the correct place to author new origin research — it becomes the write-path for origin.*, not a dataset generators read directly.

Same status as compatibility-explanation-variants.json, for the sibling-harmony renderer.

A small, closed, curated set (27 anchors). Could remain a standalone lookup table indefinitely (status 'keep' would also be defensible) or be merged onto each anchor's own entity record — a judgment call for a future migration-planning phase, not resolved here.
A scoring ruleset (factors + patterns), not per-entity data. Continues to exist as config that a canonical-model-aware compatibility function would read, not as entity data itself.
